title: SpectraFlux: Harnessing the Flow of Multi-FPGA in Mass Spectrometry Clustering
problem: Mass spectrometry clustering for large-scale proteomic datasets is computationally intensive, with single-device accelerators bottlenecked by memory bandwidth and compute capacity. Inter-FPGA communication overhead and variable data rates in adaptive clustering complicate multi-device scaling.
motivation: Mass spectrometry-based protein identification and quantification is foundational to proteomics, providing critical insights into biological systems and disease states.
method: SpectraFlux employs heterogeneous clustering kernels with adaptive bucket-size management across multiple FPGAs using the TAPA-CS framework for automatic dataflow compilation and partitioning. Memory usage is optimized by distinguishing on-chip and high-bandwidth memory (HBM) storage. A refined frame-based cost model for inter-FPGA communication via RDMA accommodates variable data rates inherent in proteomic processing.
key_novelty: Frame-based cost model for inter-FPGA communication that adapts to variable proteomic data rates, reducing inter-FPGA data movement by 73% in multi-FPGA clustering.
contributions: Multi-FPGA heterogeneous clustering architecture achieving 2.7X speedup on quad-FPGA vs single FPGA
Adaptive bucket-size kernels optimizing memory allocation between on-chip and HBM storage
Refined frame-based cost model for inter-FPGA communication reducing data movement 73%
Integration with TAPA-CS framework enabling automatic dataflow compilation across multiple FPGAs

metrics.speedup: 2.7X (quad-FPGA vs single-FPGA), 11X vs SOTA FPGA, 17X vs GPU
